And if this is the case, then it is up to the party presenting that piece of evidence to prove its authenticity. And if we will be having a discussion on this, I will make a written filing on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, the next document is P 00081. It's in the same binder. Now, do you recognise this, sir, as the original decision on establishing the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna dated the 18th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a decision to set up the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna under that number, the decision as it was published in the Official Gazette of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. In other words, it's not the text -- we had two texts here, one before the Tribunal and the other that was passed on the 18th of November, 1992, and we had this decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which was amended by virtue of the 3rd of July decision of the Presidency. In other words, the -- what I have is the decision of -- as it was published in the Official Gazette following these amendments. I don't know if this is true for you as well, if you have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let's break it down. Can we agree that there are two decisions on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the original decision and then the amended decision that was passed during the Presidency meeting in July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And it's my belief or it's my hope anyway that what you should have in front of you is the initial decision, that's the first decision not the amended one. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. There must be a misunderstanding here because I know that in e-court under that number in the English version we have the original decision, whereas in the B/C/S we have the 3rd of July decision, so that both the witness and the Prosecutor are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I appreciate the clarification. Perhaps what I could do -- I don't know what the -- well, let's do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me come back to this one. We will get the correct Serbo-Croatian version of this document and come back to it, Mr. Buntic, because I don't want, obviously, to ask you about it without it being in front of you. So let's move on for the time being to the next document which is P 00152 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm a bit confused because the document here in the binder in Croatian bears also the date of the 18th November 1991. Would the amended version of July be dated in the introductory paragraph 18 November 1991?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the Croatian version only refers to the fact that the original decision was passed on the 18th of November and but that it was amended on the 3rd of July and that now the consolidated text was being published. If you want, the witness can read the preamble of the decision he has in front of him and then you'll see where the difference lies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Please, yes. Would you read in Croatian the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The decision" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think you should start -- you should start on the top of the page with [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I started reading the preamble, which in my view solves the question that was put, Your Honour. The question was put about the 18th of November and the 3rd of July, which is why I started reading the part of the preamble which sheds light on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have before me a document which has a number at the bottom and the number is 00299117. Do you have the same document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have this document in front of me on the screen, but in the binder, as I've already indicated, I have a different document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher can assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We can provide the witness with a hard copy of the -- okay. That clarifies it. He's not in the correct document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's fine. Now I have in front of me the original dated the 18th of November, 1991, and it begins with the words: "On the basis of the freely expressed will of the Croat people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, they are democratically ..." So that would be the first document, and if you allow me to provide an explanation by way of answer to His Honour's question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, I think we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think that is quite all right. We have now identified the document and that was all I was wondering about. Thank you. Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, I wanted to then ask you if you would for us read the first sentence of Article 2, just read it in your language, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 2: "The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna shall comprise the territories of the following municipalities: Jajce, Kresevo, Busovaca" --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. You don't need to read out the names of the municipalities. I want to now skip down to Article 7 because this relates to the organization or the governmental structures of Herceg-Bosna, and this indicates that: "The supreme authority of the Community," the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, "shall be the Presidency ..." And my question is this: You indicated earlier in your testimony that really throughout the entire period -- well, I'll ask you. Is it true that from this period, in November 1991 continuing through 1992 and 1993, the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was a single-party Presidency, that is, it was a party -- it was a Presidency constituted by an -- exclusively by members of the Croatian Democratic Union party?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This follows from the heading of this document, or rather, the preamble that speaks about the democratically elected representatives of the Croatian people elected as such into the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And as is quite well-known in the elections of Bosnia and Herzegovina there were parties such as my own that did not get a single seat in the Assembly of the republic. So we're talking about the representatives elected by the Croatian people who were at the same time all members of the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So in order to be on the Presidency one had to be a member of the Croatian Democratic Union?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, one had to be elected. So the criterion is not membership of the Croatian Democratic Union; the criterion is that these people had to have been elected into the bodies, those bodies. So the key term here is "elected representatives of the Croatian people," not members of the Croatian Democratic Union. So the key language here is "democratically elected," not the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And these democratic elections occurred when? Tell us when they occurred and where.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late 1990, the first democratic elections were held in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So it was on the basis of those elections that then the membership or the same results of that election, if you will, were the basis of membership then in the Presidency of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I presented my interpretation or my view of the preamble of this decision, where it says the democratically elected representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, getting back to my original question on this, is it true that throughout the remainder of 1991, 1992, and 1993, all members of the Presidency were members of the Croatian Democratic Union; correct or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure but I think there were some representatives in the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna who were not members of the Croatian Democratic Union. As far as I know, the representative from the Vares municipality was a member of the Party of Democratic Movement, and I think there were some other Presidency members who were co-opted at a later stage and who were there as members of the HZ HB Presidency; I can't now recall their names. I think that there was this man from Vares, he participated in the meetings, and I know that he was a member of the SDP. There were some other examples of that nature but I can't recall them. So it was not a single-party body.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you're changing your testimony from earlier in which you said that it's a single-party Presidency? I can refer you to the relevant part of your testimony if you like.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can confirm that now. When it was established pursuant to this fundamental document, that was the case. But then I added that some members had been co-opted at a later stage and that they had participated in the work, I think it was Petar Ravlija, I can't recall, but at any rate it was a representative from Vares and I know that there was a man from the SDP. So he was co-opted at a later stage. He did not participate in the work of the Presidency right at the beginning, but I can confirm, as I have before, that all the founding members were members of the HDZ, but later on some other members of the Presidency joined in and they were not members of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: These other members of the Presidency, did they join in before or after the 17th of October, 1992, which was the last time the Presidency met?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was even before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So if in fact they are members of the Presidency, presumably their names would be evident on the minutes of the Presidency meetings that occurred during these times in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it would be good to look at the minutes from the meeting of the Presidency dated the 17th of October, 1992, held in Travnik where the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was joined by other communities, Bosnian Posavina, Central Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the Soli community, where representatives or members of those communities were co-opted and became members of the Presidency. Unfortunately, after that time the Presidency never met again, but I think you can see from the minutes who were the signatories and who attended that meeting or that session on the 17th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And we will be going over the minutes of the meetings, both on the 17th of October and also the July meeting as well. So we will get to that. Now the next document I would like to show you, Mr. Buntic, is P 00152, it's behind the tab called 152 in your binder. Now, we've just been looking at the initial establishment of Herceg-Bosna dated 18th of November, 1991. This document follows a little bit after that, making reference to an emergency session of the Presidency on the 8th of April, 1992, and this decision, if you have it, is the decision on the creation of the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct and I've already stated before this Court that this is one of the documents that was handed to me on the 20th of June when I took over my duty, and I can confirm that this is one of those documents and I have it here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And in this document the HVO was named to be the supreme defence body of the Croatian people in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, your quotation from Article 1 was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And at all times throughout the remainder of 1992 and 1993, the HVO remained the supreme defence body of the Croatian people in the HZ HB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. But I don't think that we should now embark upon an analysis of the civilian and military segments because this was not at issue then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to get there as well. The next document is P 00206, 206 in your binder. Now, Mr. Buntic, this appears to be about five weeks after the decision establishing the HVO as the supreme defence body. This is a decision dated the 15th of May, 1992, which relates to the provisional establishment of the executive authority, executive authority, and administration in the territory of Herceg-Bosna. And is it true, sir, that then this document indicates or provides that the HVO now shall carry out the duties of the executive authority in the territory of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but I have to say that the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna operated under the same title or name, so it should be noted here, this difference, it would be proper to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. For those of us who weren't there, though, for us to read this, would you agree with me that one could logically conclude based on the documents that as of this time, the 15th of May, 1992, both supreme defence authority and executive authority was vested in the same body called the HVO? You need to give an audible answer so we can get it in the record.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can agree with you on that, and that's what I've already stated before this Tribunal, that this is how it worked until the regulations were changed, until the establishment of the Croatian Defence Council as the executive civilian body that got its president at the session of the 14th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on Article 3 of this document, P 00206, we again see that -- an indication that the Presidency has a position of supremacy in that the HVO is to report to the Presidency; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then continuing, this indicates that: "The president of the HVO and the vice-presidents, the heads of departments, shall all -- shall be collectively responsible for the decisions adopted by the HVO." Did that remain so throughout 1992 and 1993, that is, collective responsibility of the HVO and its members for the decisions taken by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that portions of Article 3 were amended pursuant to the decision on the establishment of the Croatian Defence Council, but before this decision was issued, Article 3 was in force in full, as it stands here in this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And we will get to the subsequent decision amending this, so I will take you to that in a few minutes. My last question on this document, Mr. Buntic, is in Article 7, which is the article that identifies or sets out the specific departments, the administrative departments, of the HVO. And what I found interesting here was that there was no justice department provided. There's a department of general administration, but there's no reference to a justice department. And I just was sort of curious about that then, because we will see that in fact a department of justice and general administration was established in the subsequent amendment, and I take that that's because during this intervening period you then became the head and took up your responsibilities as head of that department. Would you just comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to you and to my colleague, Mr. Stringer, but I think that this is a case of misinterpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something? I'm not sure, Mr. Prosecutor, that we are indeed talking about the same document. The document that I have in front of me, it's in Croatian, statutory decision dated the 18th of November, 1991. In Article 7 it stipulates that there should be department of justice and general administration and other departments. So to my mind this is a correct transcription or a copy of the original statutory decision, and I had the opportunity to see it in the original. And Article 7 here envisages the department of justice and general administration. I don't know how this is translated into English. My English is not good enough for me to be able to verify that, but perhaps the registry and the Prosecution and the Defence might check whether this is the same document, or perhaps we're talking about incomplete or incorrect translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So then your -- if I understand correctly, your understanding -- your testimony then is that there was indeed a department or -- a department of justice and general administration within the HVO from its very inception?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and that follows from the document that I have in front of me, that you handed to me, the Prosecution handed this document to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next document -- actually, it's not a document. Mr. Buntic, I'm just going to ask you to set aside the binder for a minute because we're going to watch a little bit of video footage. I'm going to ask you some questions about the Presidency meeting that occurred in July of 1992, I believe it was the 3rd of July. And you were shown this video footage during the Kordic case, which was a long time ago, but my understanding was that you believed this was footage showing a part of the Presidency meeting that took place in July of 1992. This is P 10518. It's about one and a half minutes, one and one-half minutes in length. It's not very lengthy, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The necessity for bringing certain regulations or filling legal voids that developed with decision of organs or bodies of the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina has shown itself. Instead of a Law on Armed Forces or a Law on All People's Defence, an order was issued on the armed forces of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna and the decision on the rights and obligations of members of the Croatian Defence Council, a decree on the assumption of ownership of the JNA and SSNO logistics in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, a decree on the transfer of ownership of property of the occupier, and a decree on public reparations. "With the bringing of these regulations as well as other regulations that the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna has passed, the conditions for the normal functioning and other aspects of life have been created."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The sound quality was really very bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. I don't have any questions for you about that, Mr. Buntic, other than just to ask you: Do you recognise that as footage of the time during the period of the 3 July 1992 Presidency meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct, it's my image and my voice. I think that this is a press conference that followed immediately after the session of the Presidency of the 3rd of June, or rather, July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where did that Presidency meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hotel in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I think we saw some images on there. Mr. Boban was present. I recognised Dario Kordic as another one of the people who were present. So it's fair to say that the Presidency was fairly fully constituted or present at this particular meeting in July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure if all the members were there. I know that the large majority of the members of the Presidency were there, and it is true, you were able to recognise those people. I saw the late Boban. I recognised Dario Kordic and some other members of the Presidency -- well, I don't know them but what you just said is true, Boban and Kordic were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And now at this particular Presidency meeting it strikes me as being a fairly important one. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were a total of five sessions of the Presidency of the HZ HB, and to my mind all of them were equally important because major decisions were issued at each of those sessions for the first of all survival, or rather, first of all for the establishment and later on for the functioning of the Croatian Community. So I think that each and every one of them was important.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: One of the decisions adopted at this Presidency meeting was the decision to amend and amending the decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true. This is the document that we've just mentioned, so the basic decision of the 18th of November, 1992, was amended at the session and the text, the integral version of the text, was then published in the Official Gazette of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this is July of 1992, and as I understand from your testimony, by this point you were actually involved as a member of the HVO. You had assumed your position as head of the justice department by this time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. As I've just noted, some 10 or 12 days before that, as I said I assumed my duties on the 20th or the 21st of July -- of June, and this is the 3rd of July, so that was about 10 or 12 days after I assumed my duties at the post.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you personally involved in drafting the amendments to this decision?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I participated in the drafting of the amendments to those decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I want to ask you, first of all, about some words that appear in the preamble or the reasons in this decision, this amended decision, establishing the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. This is P 00078, 078.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. Let me go back to the video footage. I have two related questions, they're not major but they might be interesting, I think. I note, first of all, that there is a big meeting table with basically only men. How is it that there was not even one woman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honour, well, a meeting would probably be a much more pleasant and nicer occasion had that been the case, but as we could see the founding members of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, those who established it on the 18th of November, were all men and also the secretary of the Presidency was also a man. I think his name was Zeljko Galic. I don't recall who kept the minutes, but yes, of course, the picture would have been that much nicer had there been any women there, in the frame at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. On that footage, but things go very quickly, we see this meeting room, this large meeting room with people dressed in civilian clothes and we see a few individuals dressed in military clothes. But I noted that there was a second table. There were two tables, probably the most prominent people were sitting at the main table, and next to that table there was another table probably for the assistants of the others. Can you confirm that? Can you confirm that on top of these leading officials of the HVO there were at these meetings -- this meeting their assistants, their secretaries, what have you, who were sitting at this second table. Is that what we see on the video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we went back to the footage now I would probably recognise some of the individuals. Judging from what I was able to see at that moment, I believe that sitting at one of the tables were journalists, the ones we were able to see in civilian clothes. I think I saw two journalists among them. What we saw was a brief information intended for the general public after the Presidency meeting. And as you saw, I was authorised to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The best is probably to view the footage again. It may prove significant because we have here the names of the people who attended that meeting, but we may identify other people. So I'd like us to view this footage again, to play the video again, because I didn't get the impression that these people were journalists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see you, you're holding a press conference, and here we have this frame where we see the main table and a table next to it. We see it here with someone turning his back to us. Would that be the journalists sitting at this particular table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I was referring to a moment ago. I think that sitting at the table which is on the right-hand side as we're looking at the video there were journalists who attended the Presidency meeting on the 3rd of July. We can continue playing the footage, and perhaps I might recognise someone. But I believe that the individuals seated at the table on the right-hand side are journalists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I put the question: Does one not see right of the head of the person with a blue -- man with a blue sweater or something, a microphone? It looks to me a bit like a microphone on a socle and that would then not fit with the hypothesis that these are journalists.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I wasn't sure but that I thought that they were journalists because I know that journalists were present. When I was looking at the footage as it was played a moment ago, I believed that I recognised one of the journalists. His name is Blasko, I can't recall his family name at this time. He was a correspondent of the Croatian television, I believe. The other time when we were watching a clip I recognised him. And I said that I was certain that I saw some journalists -- well, in fact, I saw him but I am sure that there were others too. Perhaps his name was Blasko Raguz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we can finish playing the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is not my intention to testify, but what Judge Trechsel saw is something that I thought I saw and my colleagues confirm it, it was a bottle, testifying again to the presence of men only, otherwise there might not have been a bottle there. At any rate, we believe it is a bottle, not a microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's continue with the footage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I can't identify this individual at that moment. I dare not speculate. I wouldn't want to make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. For the record I would like to specify that at some point in the video we saw people shopping, going shopping, and paying with bank notes. I don't know if these were Croatian dinars, Deutschemarks, or whatever -- no, but we saw bank notes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm being told it may be time for a break. I could continue, we could break now; as you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We are back in session. Mr. Stringer, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, you should have in front of you Exhibit P 00078, which is the amended decision of 3 July 1992 on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just before the break I had asked you, and you had indicated yes, that you were involved in drafting some of the language in this decision, although you did not indicate which parts you were involved with. I take it you were involved in the drafting of this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, I want to direct your attention to one part of the preamble, the third paragraph of the preamble, which begins with the words: "Pursuant to the Constitution of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina ..." And it continues on with various recitations. There's a reference to the inexhaustive right of peoples to self-determination and sovereignty, including the right to association. And this is the part I want to ask you about: "And pursuant to the unacceptability of the unitary state model and multi-ethnic societies, the Croat people ..." and then it continues on to indicate "... shall establish the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." This passage: "Pursuant to the unacceptability of the unitary state model and multi-ethnic societies ..." I'm going to take you to one or two other documents in a few moments, but let me just ask you, sir, those words there, are those your words? Is that a reflection of your input into this part of the decision?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the third paragraph should be looked at in the context of the entirety of the document and not isolated. The third paragraph is somewhat longer and contains other statements as well. It is true that I was a member of the working group that drafted this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm -- would you perhaps look again at the -- or remember the question. The question was whether you had drafted these words, not whether this was a long paragraph or what it meant or what the context was, but just whether you had drafted it and that can be answered by yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot answer with a yes or no because I said that I participated in the group which drafted this document; in other words, I was not working on it on my own. I said that I was a member of the group which prepared the text, and as you know, the Presidency decided to adopt this decision with the text as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me take you to a different document and then I'll bring you back to this. In the fourth binder, number 4, 1D 01670, if the usher could assist. The fourth binder, 1D 01670. Mr. Buntic, this document is the minutes of this Presidency meeting of the 2nd of July, 1993. And if you go through this document you will see that item number 2 relates to the decision amending the decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And -- actually, just to back up a little bit, I'm looking at the fourth page of the English version. The minutes are reporting the statements of various members and people who are present, and item number 8 relates to a statement by Mr. Blago Artukovic. And then underneath that there's a reference to a statement of you, Mr. Buntic. And Mr. Artukovic had said that the SDA and their leaders -- do you have that part of the document in front of you, Mr. Buntic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. If you find on page -- I'll take you to page -- the relevant page of the Serbo-Croatian version, it's the -- begins at the bottom of a page that ends with the letter -- the number 0455. Do you see 1D 32-0455, the bottom left -- right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. So Mr. Artukovic begins speaking, and then on the next page there is a reference with your name and that's the part I'm going to ask you about now. Mr. Artukovic says that the SDA and their leaders were advocating a unitary Bosnia-Herzegovina known as a civic one and would not renounce that principle. And he said the people were inadequately informed of the work and the organization of the HVO and the HZ HB. And then at this point you said that in reference to his comments that you, Mr. Buntic, "explained that nowhere in the world was there a state which was at once unitary and multi-ethnic. The HZ HB endorsed this principle and any other manner of work and organization would merely be an experiment such as the former SFRY," the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, "was." So that's what made me ask you a couple of minutes ago, whether these words which somehow found their way into the preamble of the amended decision actually were your words because you seem to be saying just that very same thing here as reflected in the minutes, the view that a unitary state model and a multi-ethnic society is unacceptable. So I'll ask you then again. Those words to the extent they're found in the preamble of the amended decision, are those your words? Did you write that or did you introduce those words into the preamble with the approval, obviously, of the membership of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that the minutes correctly reflect what I said at the time, that is, the views reflected in the transcript were mine and were accurately reported. I also said that I participated in the group which developed the amendments to the decision establishing the HZ HB. The views contained in the minutes were mine and were correctly conveyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And just a couple questions about your views on that, sir. Is it your view or was it your view at this time -- well, let me ask you this: In terms of a unitary state, what do you mean by that? By that do you mean a state in which, as we say, there is one man/one vote?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did mean that, but I also had in mind the multi-ethnic communities such as exist in the world. There are many confederal states or multi-ethnic communities which have confederal or a federal system. As I stated here, I wasn't aware of a single case anywhere in the world where a multi-ethnic community would be organized on the unitary principle or it can be translated into the principle of one man/one vote. We know that Slobodan Milosevic advocated this principle and stood by it firmly. In my view, this was the reason why the former Yugoslavia was broken up and dissolved, because it was a multi-ethnic community which could not work on that principle. The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is also a multi-ethnic community, and as such -- and it was defined as such in Article 1 of its constitution. Since we had had the experience of the multi-ethnic Yugoslavia having been broken up which there were attempts to organize on that principle of one man/one vote, I believed that this principle would not be appropriate for the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as a multi-ethnic community. In my view, the future Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Bosnia-Herzegovina that had only just been internationally recognised, could not be organized based on that principle. This was also consistent with the views expressed by the Badinter Commission, views which had already been made public by that time. This was, therefore, based on the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, on the opinions of the Badinter Commission, on the international documents prescribing the rights of peoples. I stand by the views I held at the time, and they are correctly reflected in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just qualify the fact that I wasn't the only one drafting the preamble; it was drafted by a group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the time of this amended decision in July of 1992, is it true, sir, that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was in fact a unitary state consisting of a multi-ethnic society or population?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, in its constitution Bosnia-Herzegovina was defined as a state of the Bosniak people, the Serb people, and the Croat people; therefore, as a state of three constituent peoples. What was said here was based on those same principles, and I kindly ask you to allow me to add something. In my testimony in the Kordic case, on the issue of these constitutional principles I made a statement that covered --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- 22 pages -- please allow me to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise, but I can't allow you to finish. The Trial Chamber doesn't have -- we know about your previous testimony, but we're interested in your evidence as you sit here today. We can submit your Kordic testimony if the Trial Chamber wants it, but you've got to ask -- or you've got to answer the questions that I'm asking you here today rather than the answers that you gave in the Kordic trial. This is -- I think it's a simple question, it's certainly intended to be one. Isn't it true that Bosnia-Herzegovina at this time was a multi-ethnic society based upon a unitary state model?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And so, what we're seeing is a rejection of the fundamental way in which the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina was organized in -- as of July of 1992, that model was not acceptable to you and the others who wrote and adopted this amended decision; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, is it true then that what you - and I'll use what we call the royal you, if I may - you and the other leaders of Herceg-Bosna who were writing this, what you wanted was rather a territory, a unit that was governed by Croatian people?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, Mr. Prosecutor, the decision establishing the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, or rather, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was not set up on state territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina because at the time of the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not exist. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was set up in the territory of what was at the time the dissolving Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the opinion of, number one, the Badinter Commission --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I don't think you're answering my question, sir, with respect. This is my question, I'm asking about now July of 1992. We've established that you and your colleagues writing this decision rejected or would not accept -- do not accept the unitary state model for Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'll ask you an open-ended question. What is it that you wanted? Tell us, what did you want instead?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We advocated a Bosnia-Herzegovina as a compound state of three constituent peoples which would have mechanisms aimed at protecting the rights of all three constituent peoples. As you are well aware, the Croatian negotiating delegation accepted all the three models for the resolution of the BH crisis offered by the international community. All of the models offered were based on the principles I have referred to and the principles that I was in favour of, that the state should be organized as a community of all the three constituent peoples. Already at that time a unitary model of Bosnia-Herzegovina was unacceptable to all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then you wanted a model in which there would be three constituent units, if I may use the word, a Muslim unit, a Serb unit, and a Croatian or a Croat unit, is that correct, all within the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all times [Realtime transcript read in error "At all times"]. As is well-known, the Cutileiro Plan was not based on the three territorial units, nor was the Vance-Owen Plan - please let me finish - in the drafting of which I also participated because it was not based on the three constituent units. The Owen-Stoltenberg Plan was based on the three constituent units. The Washington Agreement was based on two constituent units as well as the Dayton Accords, that is to say, they were based on two constituent units. Therefore, Bosnia-Herzegovina was organized as a compound state of two constituent units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. But I'm just asking: What did you want? I'm not interested in what the international community wanted or was proposing. I'm simply asking you to tell us what you wanted, and specifically did you want there to be three constituent units or entities within Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was very precise and said that the Croat side had accepted all the plans offered it. Now, what somebody intended to do or wished to do within one's own territory is something that I cannot gauge. I can only tell you the views that were expressed. Now, what somebody intended to do or thought of doing is something that my profession doesn't allow me to speculate on. I said that all the international plans for Bosnia-Herzegovina offered by the international community to resolve the Bosnian-Herzegovinian crisis were accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could just say -- just to correct the record not to intervene, on page 70, line 18, the gentleman indicated, "Not at all times." It doesn't reflect that in the record, so perhaps that could be clarified. That was the response to the question, "Not at all times." That is what my colleague heard, in English that is what I heard, but that wasn't reflected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, the time I'm interested in is the 3rd of July, 1992, and I think that you're actually extremely well-qualified and positioned, Mr. Buntic, to tell us what it was that the leadership of Herceg-Bosna wanted. At this time when it was rejecting the unitary state model for Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you want to have a Croatian entity or a unit in which there was a territory that would be governed by the Croatian people, and equally so, other territories and units that could be governed by the Muslims for their part and the Serbs as well? Isn't that what you wanted, that the people should have their own space, the three peoples?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you're a lawyer by profession, as am I. In my earlier answer I said that I don't know and am not allowed to say what somebody thought or wanted. I can only speak about the deeds, and I did speak about it. All the peace plans were accepted. These are facts. That's something I can talk about. If I talked about what somebody wanted or thought, I would enter into a realm of conjecture and surmise, which I don't believe is relevant to this case. Besides, I don't consider myself competent to speak about these matters; they rather fall into the field of psychology and not law.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, I prefer talking about facts and deeds rather than thoughts or wishes of individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you testified in the Kordic case, Mr. Buntic, you did -- you were more willing to express at least your personal view at that time. Looking at page 21123 of the Kordic transcript, and this is what you were asked. This is the question from the Prosecutor to you in that case. "Q. The one point I wanted to ask: The division of Bosnia into three ethnic groups, as it were, under Owen-Stoltenberg, that is not substantially different, is it, from the basic cantonal division of the party, the Croatian Democratic Party, I believe, that you were initially -- or that you were a member of. In other words, the three divided ethnic groups was pretty much the pattern that you saw as appropriate for Bosnia; is that correct?" And your answer to that question was: "If you're asking me for my personal position, I still believe that this was the best plan for Bosnia and Herzegovina, yes." So is that your view, sir, and I'll ask you your personal view then since you're not comfortable speaking about the views of the Herceg-Bosna leadership, was it your own view that the three nationalities, if you will, should be separated and divided within Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again in your question there is a trap which prevents me from giving you a yes or no answer. So it was not about the division of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that's why I can't give you a yes or no answer. We're talking about the way in which Bosnia and Herzegovina was to be structured on the basis of the principle with three constituent peoples. And I maintain what I said in the Kordic case, but again I presented my own views, my own position, not views or positions of other peoples. So I'm fully consistent in what I'm saying. I'm saying the same thing that I said in the Kordic case, and I still think, I still hold, that this was the best plan for Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is my opinion. That's my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just so we're talking -- just to we're clear, I want to make it absolutely clear then what it is that you're expressing as your personal view. You're saying that three divided ethnic groups --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the question. I don't need to hear the rest of it. Excuse me, sir. I don't need to hear the rest of it. This has been asked and it's been answered. Now since he doesn't like it, he's trying to twist and turn and formulate a question or put words into the witness's mouth. Might I remind the Trial Chamber that it was the international community that came up with the plans. Are we indicting the international community? If so, let's put them in in the indictment; if not, let's move on. I think it's been asked and it's been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I disagree. I don't think I'm getting a straight answer or a sufficient answer on this, and I just think it's necessary for the record to be clear what it is the witness said. If he wants to talk about a plan, that's great; if he wants to -- I'm asking him his personal view --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Whether in your own personal view ethnic separation, ethnic division among the three groups, was the best solution for Bosnia-Herzegovina, because that's what I read your testimony as in the Kordic case. We can all look at the transcript and read it for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if he wants the entire transcript of the Kordic case to be admitted, we have no objections. In fact, we fully appreciate it having it been admitted. Now, how many times does he need to ask the question? He's been asked it, he answered it. He's never indicated anything about separation. He's talking about the internal division inside Bosnia-Herzegovina on a political basis so that three constituent nations can live among themselves and enjoy equal status and equal rights. He said that over and over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We can tender the transcript, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the Prosecutor is asking you for your personal view on the issue of ethnic separation into three groups. He's asking you for your personal opinion. Please state it, it's not that complicated. Were you in favour of it or against it? Is that a mistake in the transcript? You're bound to have a personal view.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is my opinion that I did present my views quite accurately and with some precision. So it is my opinion that the internal organization of Bosnia-Herzegovina with the three constituent units was the best solution or is the best solution for Bosnia and Herzegovina. I cannot accept or I cannot even answer a question that has to do with the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina because we're not talking about the division, we're talking about the internal organization. So I think that I was quite clear and precise in my answer when I said that it was my opinion, my position, that Bosnia and Herzegovina should be set up on the basis of three constituent units. That's what I advocated. I wasn't talking about the division, so I cannot accept this imposition in the form of a question about the division when all I'm talking about is the internal organization. I don't know if I have made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's answered the question. In his view, the organization had to take into account the existence of these three ethnic groups. That's what you said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And so within the intact borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because I'm not talking about a division of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I'm talking about the way in which it's organized within its borders, this is my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Stringer, I think this question now really was answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: The President asked and that answer I think really settles it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Buntic, if you could go back to the binder that's on the bottom, back to the amended decision establishing Herceg-Bosna. And if I could direct you, sir, to Article 2. If I could just ask you again to read the first passage -- read Article 2 up until the beginning of the list of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 2: "The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna shall comprise the territories of the municipalities ..." I don't know if you wanted me to go on or to stop here where the names of the municipalities are listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, that's fine because we can all read the names of the municipalities. Now, my first question is: As from the first decision in November of 1991 to now this amended decision in July of 1992, do you know if there was any changes made to the listing of municipalities that's found here or did that listing remain the same?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, the list remained the same until the 17th of October, 1992, when some other communities joined this community, Posavina, Soli --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and Usora, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. But within the initial Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna there was no change?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the listing of municipalities here we have two that are unique in that there is some brackets or parenthesis that is after them. For example, Skender Vakuf, there's a reference to Dobratici and then at the end for the municipality of Trebinje, there is a reference to Ravno. And as I understand it, those two municipalities are unique in that the parts of those municipalities that's referred to are only those specific parts, that is, for Skender Vakuf it's only the Dobratici area that is a part of the Croatian Community and not the entirety of the municipality of Skender Vakuf; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is correct, but I think that we need to note here that in paragraph 1 of this article we're talking about the territories of the municipalities. I want to stress that the term territory is not the same as the term territory, "podrucje" and "teritorija." These two terms have different meanings in Croatian, in everyday language. If you're talking about the territory of a municipality, you're talking about the overall area, "podrucje," of a municipality. And if you're talking about "podrucje," area, then it does not mean the entire territory of the municipality. So in Croatian language these two terms have a different meaning. I gave you the meanings in everyday parlance, but I think that I've already explained that I'm not a linguist and I couldn't give you an expert opinion. But I presented the view as to what those terms mean in everyday language in Croatian. Now, I don't know how one should translate that into English. I don't know whether the translation into English has been correct, but I've explained to you what those terms mean in everyday Croatian language and parlance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: With your permission, Mr. President, I'd like to put up a map that is in evidence that indicates the ethnic composition of the municipalities not just of Herceg-Bosna but of Bosnia-Herzegovina in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you see the map on the screen in front of you, Mr. Buntic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I can tell you that if you can see the blue border that runs throughout the middle sections of the map and then the blue border again that runs across the north-eastern section, those are representing the borders of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the border of the Croatian Community of the Posavina in the north-eastern part. So that's what the blue borders relate to. And I'm going to ask you about the areas within the borders of Herceg-Bosna. Would you agree with me, sir, that within the territory or the municipalities that are listed in Article 2 of this decision there is a great deal of ethnic diversity?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is great ethnic diversity, but I think that in the areas as they are indicated here, the Croatian people would be in the majority, that's one thing; and I think that there's no need to trick me by showing me those borders because it's nothing but a trick. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna never published or shown a map that would show the borders of the Croatian Community. So if you want me to confirm this map in this sense, I cannot do it because the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna did not have its borders.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true, sir, that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, as it says in this decision, it consisted of or comprised these municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me be quite specific and tell you what the decision says. Areas, "podrucje," of these municipalities, not the overall, the total territory of those municipalities. I can't give you a different answer. If anyone else can, let them do that, but I cannot and indeed no other answer can be derived from this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. So then it's your testimony, sir, that the territory, if you will, the space - I'm trying to use a neutral word - of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna only extended to parts of these municipalities but not these municipalities in their entirety?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be a more correct interpretation. So not the total, overall territory of those municipalities, but just some areas in those municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This document, however, doesn't give us any indication of which areas would then fall within the territory or the jurisdiction of Herceg-Bosna with the exception of Trebinje and Skender Vakuf; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is indicated in Article 2 of the decision is correct, and I can't really interpret it in any other way nor is it possible to give it any other interpretation that would be in the spirit of the Croatian language. So we're talking about the areas of the municipalities listed here, not the territories. You see Ravno and Trebinje and Dobratici listed here, and I can give you an explanation as to why but it is not necessary. If you want me to do so, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, I think we know about that. I don't think it's necessary for you to give an explanation on those too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, we're on map 9 which is part of Exhibit P 09276.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me move on to just another part of this document, Mr. Buntic, Article 7 which relates to the organization, if you will, of the governing bodies of Herceg-Bosna. You see here that the president of the Croatian -- we're talking about the supreme authority vested first in the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, we know that was Mr. Boban who was the Commander-in-Chief as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then there's a reference: "... or also vested in the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which shall consist of representatives of the Croatian people in the municipal bodies of authority, the senior official thereof, or the presidents of the municipal Croatian Defence Council." And then it goes on to say that: "The Presidency then ... would be the legislative body of the HZ HB." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. You quoted this part of Article 7 correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then just on to Article 8, it's the Presidency, then, that shall appoint the executive and administrative bodies?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And would we agree that this is a reference, then, to the HVO, which is the executive part of the leadership or governance of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, Mr. Prosecutor, because the civilian HVO was established after this amended decision was passed as an executive body of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, getting back up to Article 7 on the Presidency, is it true, sir, that only Croatian people could be a member of the Presidency of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct because the wording here did not exclude other possibilities, because presidents of the municipal HVO, so I'm talking about paragraph 2 that you've just read, the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which shall consist of representatives of the Croatian people in the municipal authorities which would confirm your argument or presidents of the Croatian Defence Council who need not be Croats. They could come from other ethnic groups. So the way it is worded, it does not exclude the possibility that non-Croats could participate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is it true, though, in fact that there were no Muslim members of the Presidency and there were no Muslims who were presidents of the municipal HVOs during 1992 and up until August of 1993 when the Croatian Community changed into the Croatian republic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part of your question or your argument I can confirm, but not the second part. So I'm not sure, and I think that there were some examples where Bosniaks were presidents of the HVO. I'm not sure, but there were such cases. We saw here some evidence called before this Court, including a document from the Stolac municipality to the Republic of Croatia seeking assistance in the effort to get arms. I'm not sure whether this document was drafted or signed by the representative or the president of the HVO or the Party of Democratic Action. So I can't give you an answer to the second part of your question. So it was possible that somebody -- that non-Croats could be presidents of the HVO. Now, whether this was so in practice, I don't know, but it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Moving you back to Article 1 of this decision, Mr. Buntic, if you could just explain this in light of your previous remarks about the municipalities or parts of municipalities that were falling within the HZ HB. Article 1 indicates that: "The HZ HB shall be established as a political, cultural, economic, and territorial whole." Now, that's how the linguists give it to me in English. Clearly I don't know how now hear it in your language, but that certainly would imply, sir, that there is a territorial aspect to this entity called Herceg-Bosna. Isn't that true, there was a territory, a physical land, territory, of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it couldn't just hang there up in the air. Once again let me remind you, we're not talking about territories we're talking about areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would like to say and ask the witness that even if the two Croatian words are, let's say, different as far as the territory and the space or whatever are concerned, but I really believe that the witness cannot claim that it cannot be -- in a way it cannot be determined as far as the territorial entity is concerned and we all know that there was a territorial entity which was later on called the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and it is also my question, therefore, that when we saw previous documents it was a very categorical reference that this Croatian entity has a territorial meaning as well. I do not have it before me, but I believe that before the break we had this document to be shown and you spoke about it. So therefore I would like to ask you that: Do you claim that there was no territorial integral part of the Croatian territory of first the HDZ and later on, of course, the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna? Do you agree with this or would you like to say that because of the two expressions in Croatian you claim that there is not a single territorial entity which was called as Herceg-Bosna or the territory of the HDZ. That is my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as is quite well-known every community must be based on some area or territory. I don't think there should be any misunderstandings about that. There is a misunderstanding between the question asked by the Prosecution and my answers and it is this. There was an area that was the area of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, but this did not include municipalities with their total territories. What this term meant was just parts of those municipalities. So it could refer to the overall territory of the municipalities of Citluk, Tomislavgrad, and Ljubuski, and parts of some other municipalities because the term "podrucje," area, does not necessarily mean that this was an entire territory of this municipality. But the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, I'm not denying that it had the area. It covered a certain area, but it never had borders because they were never established. So you cannot talk about the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and it would not be proper for me to talk about something that never existed, that never was. And if we're talking about the Croatian Community, later on Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, which never had its borders defined, it was always indicated that this would be established once an international agreement was in place. So that is why it is not correct to speak about the territory because territories imply borders, and here we're using the terms area, not territory of municipalities. I don't know if I have been clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, but frankly it is not very clear, I mean your answer. Of course I do not find now, in a matter of one minute or two, those documents and laws which you have promulgated and which also called for, for example, for the establishment of kind of border inspections and -- including of course the military units there and also for the customs and other services. If I am mistaken, I stand to be corrected. But as far as I know, there were indeed some units, administrative units, which had been established for that very purpose, especially because of the vulnerability of your border. So therefore, I cannot accept that there was not at all a kind of territorial entity which would have been called as Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna or later on the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. But let us not have a seminar here but the -- and the -- Mr. Stringer can proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, just to lodge an objection. I mean, it would appear with all due respect, Judge Prandler, that, one, you have formulated an opinion prior to the close of the evidence and that, one, you're calling this an entity likening it to the Republika Srpska. That troubles me. Number two, you're calling this the territory of HDZ, that's on page 84, line 1, because you equated that this is the Croatian community or territory of HDZ. I find, frankly, very alarming that you happen to have some personal views which you bring to court and somehow they get creeped into your questions, such as the one you've just indicated, that you happen to have knowledge. Having said that, it could be that things are being lost in translation, since I do know that English is your second language or third or fourth because I do know that you speak many languages. But I do wish to point out that we haven't heard all the evidence and the gentleman has indicated that we're talking about areas, areas of course -- when he said to the Prosecutor that it's not hanging up in the air. But I think to equate the HD -- the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as a territory of HDZ or an entity liking it to the Republika Srpska, which clearly had stated it goals as what it was attempting to do, which is break away from Bosnia-Herzegovina, we're talking about two different things. It would seem at this stage - and I say this with all due respect - it would appear that you are of the opinion midway through the trial that there is a para-state, a state within a state. In other words, you have bought into the Prosecution's case prior to hearing all of the evidence, and I do wish to give -- I would like for the record some clarification. And perhaps I'm being rude by asking for such clarification, I don't mean to be. I know that at times I have been less than appropriate in this courtroom, I acknowledge that, you know, but I think, with all due respect, I'm entitled to vent these issues to make sure that perhaps it is just your way of expressing yourself as opposed to holding fixed views of which then we are in somewhat of a conundrum. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. I don't want to have a very long discussion here, but I definitely refuse your qualification -- your characterization of my question and my statement in a way which was not a statement but a question explaining my question to the witness. And what I refuse was that -- and I quote here, I believe it is 14: "In other words, you have bought into the Prosecution's case prior to hearing all of the evidence ..." I definitely refuse this characterization which is hurting my independence as Judge, and it was not -- my slightest indication was not this one and therefore I refuse it. At the same time, I still -- I said I stand to be corrected. If you may prove that there was nothing which was in a way similar to kind of territorial arrangements and we have to look into all the documents and I'm sure that this issue can be settled and it was not pending in the air like Mohamed's coffin, it is not -- I'm sorry, I don't want to disturb anybody's religious feelings, but there was a territory that was an entity and nobody could tell me that this entity did not exist and nobody can tell me that this territory, however you call it, that it was not in a way a kind of tangible case there. It is quite a different question how to -- what kind of legal consequences you draw upon it. But again I say what is my major problem here is that there was certain technical sense something which could be -- which could have been called as territory, that is number one. Number two, I refuse to be characterized that I was bought in by the Prosecution. I refuse it and I thank you, Mr. Karnavas, for your very -- in a way, your statement. As you know, we are not at all enemies to each other. We are -- first of all, we are here Judges. You are there as a Defence, and therefore I would like to say that my question had been concentrated on the clarification of the territorial issue, nothing else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I meant no offence. I think if we go back to where we started, it was when Mr. Buntic was shown the map and Mr. Buntic refused to be tied in to the borders of that particular map. And there may be parts that I agree with what you've indicated, but I think Mr. Buntic was rather clear as far as what he believed when he was shown the map. Now, I'll leave it at that, Your Honours. I simply did not mean to be offensive in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, Your Honours? I also wish to express my concern with regard to some parts of what Judge Prandler said. I will focus on some issues. The witness has been telling us what he knows about the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Those of us who speak the language of the decision clearly see the difference between the terms "podrucje," area, and "teritorija," territory. The witness can speak about what the intentions of those who drafted the decision were, because had they wanted to write "territory," they would have been done so. Now, the matter that causes concern is what Judge Prandler says, that a great deal of evidence has been led about the borders and customs. As far as I know, not a single piece of evidence was led -- the evidence was led about the borders and customs between the HZ HB and the Republic of Croatia, which serves to prove that it was not the intention of the HZ HB to become a separate entity because it would not have created that border with Croatia. I do believe that this matter has not been cleared up or clarified and I hope that we shall have the opportunity to do so in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask you, Judge Antonetti, to put this question: Which territory did the HVO have in Sarajevo, Tuzla, Bihac, in the occupied Trebinje, and it was the HVO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, before my fellow Judge intervened I was about to ask you a question myself and it probably would have solved everything. Unfortunately, my fellow Judge was quicker on the mark. My question is very straightforward. Please read out in your own language Article 1 of this document. The interpreters will therefore translate exactly what is written there in your language under Article 1. Please turn to the text of the document in your language and please read out Article 1 very slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 1: "The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna shall be established as a political, cultural, economic, and territorial whole."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes, "podrucne."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you want me to give you additional explanation, I will; if not, I will stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me to interrupt, but I want to address the interpreters. We have the word "podrucne" at the end of the first -- yeah, "podrucne," and we have been told many times that territory, territorial was not a correct translation but that it must be area. Or have I got it wrong? I would really invite you to -- or tend to state if you do not agree with these linguistic questions, but I think we should avoid unnecessary difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again my fellow Judge went much faster than I did. Let me tell you what I heard from the French booth. This is what the interpreter translated and I think this is very significant. Here's what he said: "The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is created as a political, cultural, economic, and regional whole." That's what the interpreter, the French interpreter, translated. It's not exactly the same in English because in English reference is made to a whole here and not to territories or anything. So I'd like to turn to -- or I'd like to ask the following question. With respect to the word "podrucne," could you please tell us what that word means in your language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking the question to the witness. Can you please define the word "podrucne," what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For example, Bosnia and Herzegovina as a state had a single territory but several areas. We can speak about the area of Herzegovina, the area of western Herzegovina, the area of Bosnia, the area of Eastern Bosnia, the area of Western Bosnia. One territory has several areas, that's what I'm talking about, the meaning in the Croatian language. When we're talking about the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and with reference to the map that was shown earlier on, some of the communities that joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna are not visible on that map, that's the Soli community from the Tuzla area, Usora, which was also a separate area, not a contiguous area. And, for instance, Zepce, it was also dislocated. We are not talking about contiguous territory, we're talking about areas. I don't know how precise I can be in explaining this, but by trying to present the difference through examples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. If necessary the CLSS could translate Article 1 for us. It's 7.00 p.m. We'll proceed tomorrow and I don't believe that we'll conclude the testimony of the witness tomorrow. We'll have to continue on Thursday. You still have some time to spend in The Hague, Witness. It's 7.00 p.m., the hearing stands adjourned. See you tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00.
